## PM sequencing + two rulings, before any code

Recording these so the shape is auditable and the `protocol.ts` region is declared publicly.

### Region declaration — 4th concurrent editor, bounded

`canonicalMetaType` is defined in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:151`, so this fix cannot avoid the hot file. (`PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` itself lives outside it, at `packages/spec/src/shared/metadata-collection.zod.ts:111`.) Fixing `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:2938` instead is not an option: all six `/meta` entry points fold through `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` in `protocol.ts`, and REST merely duplicates the fold off the same map — a REST-only fix leaves the MCP bridge and every in-process caller open, and the `sys_metadata` row assertion is a protocol-level fact.

**Declared region: line 63 (import) + lines 124–159 (`canonicalMetaType` doc comment and body).** Disjoint from all three in-flight holders — #8268 (4264–4400), #8296 (5869–5990), #7748 (9545–14240) — and at the opposite end of the file from every one of them. Because the refusal goes *inside* `canonicalMetaType`, all six entry points inherit it with zero edits at those sites, and the ~60 inline `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` lookups never see an unfolded spelling.

This lane caps `protocol.ts` at 3 concurrent editors. I am authorising a 4th here, deliberately and on the record: the cap bounds merge thrash and semantic collision on a hot file, and an import line plus one function at the top incurs neither, while #7894 is an authorization hole with a working exploit. **The pin is the condition of the exception** — if the diff must reach outside 63 / 124–159, work stops and I re-sequence.

### Ruling 1 — the plural URL folds; it does not get its own refusal

My dispatch asked for `PUT /meta/fields/…` to become "a refusal that names the offending spelling". **That was my error.** Once the URL map is derived from `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` it necessarily contains `field -> fields`, so the plural folds to `field` and answers `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` — converging on the singular route's answer rather than producing a distinct refusal. Both defects this card names are closed by that: `200` becomes `403`, and no row is minted under `type='fields'`.

Adopting the dev's reasoning: plural REST paths are the documented legitimate spelling (`/meta/actions` folds and must keep folding), so singling out `/meta/fields/` for a spelling-refusal would give `field` a URL contract unlike every other type's, for no reason this card states — a special case in the spelling layer, which is the pattern #4432 exists to prevent. The card's third option keeps its job, scoped to spellings still unknown *after* derivation (e.g. `/meta/fieldz/`), which answer 200 today.

Corroboration worth keeping: `STATIC_REGISTRY_TYPES`' guard at `sys-metadata-repository.ts:1151` already tests both the folded singular and the raw type, so it fires correctly with **no edit of its own** once `fields` folds.

### Ruling 2 — the URL map is a UNION, not a pure derivation

A pure registry derivation silently drops seven spellings that fold correctly today and whose singular has no static registry entry — `themes`, `sharingRules`, `webhooks`, `skills`, `ragPipelines`, `analyticsCubes`, `connectors` (plus `emailTemplates`). These are plugin-registered kinds carried only by the manifest map; `protocol.code-only-types.test.ts:465` annotates `theme` verbatim as *"no static registry entry (plugin-registered)"*. A pure derivation would therefore **regress `/meta/themes`** and break this card's mandatory positive control rather than satisfy it.

So: URL map = registry-derived spellings ∪ declared irregular/camelCase spellings ∪ runtime-registered plugin kinds. Prime Directive #8's goal — *a newly **declared** type cannot arrive unmapped* — is fully served by the derived limb alone; the other limbs keep it from overreaching into a population it was never about.

The refusal is additionally to be a **purely static** rule rather than threading the live registered-type set into a module-level function, so the positive control holds *by construction* rather than by coverage. Acceptance is the invariant, not a particular predicate: **(1)** no spelling that works today may stop working, and **(2)** no unmapped spelling of a declared type may answer 200.

### Verified before any edit

The card's blast-radius table is unchanged since `bcea363` — re-derived against `origin/main`: 26 registry entries, 29 map keys, and exactly four registry types with no singular target (`field`, `seed`, `external_catalog`, `translation`, same flags). `email_template` confirmed mapped only as camelCase `emailTemplates`, with `/meta/email_templates` unmapped. `metadata-authoring-lint.ts` imports the manifest map at line 60 and iterates it at 171 and 340, so a `fields:` key would enter the walker's collection set at both — which is why option 1 stays rejected and the manifest map stays untouched.

## Correction to my own "Verified before any edit" figures

My [sequencing comment](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/7894#issuecomment-5278949907) stated, under a heading claiming verification: *"re-derived against `origin/main`: **26 registry entries**, 29 map keys."* **That count is wrong — `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` has 27 entries.** The missing one is `datasource`.

Root cause, from the dev: the pre-implementation derivation parsed the registry with a **regex over source text** rather than importing the built value. The same regex also produced the "seven dropped spellings" figure I repeated in dispatch — the real number is **six**, because `skill` *does* have a registry entry, so `skills` would have survived a pure derivation and never belonged on that list.

**What does not move:** the unmapped set is still exactly `field`, `seed`, `external_catalog`, `translation`, with the same `allowOrgOverride` / `allowRuntimeCreate` flags. The card's blast-radius table stands, mechanism assumption 2 remains confirmed, and both rulings on this card are unaffected. Everything in PR #8420 is derived from the **built** package, re-derived the moment the discrepancy surfaced, which is why the PR body says six and 27.

**Why I am posting this rather than editing quietly.** I wrote those figures under the words "Verified before any edit", which is a stronger claim than "the dev told me and I relayed it". A regex over source is not a derivation from the registry — it cannot see a re-export, a spread, or a conditional entry, and here it silently missed one. The lesson is the one this lane already learned about gate counts today and I will state it in the same form: **never quote a count you did not derive from the built value.** A number carried between a report and a ruling is a claim, and mine was unearned.

Credit where due: the dev caught this itself, on its own initiative, while reconciling a discrepancy I had only asked it to explain — and reported the root cause rather than just the corrected figure.

## Landed — `d56012f6` on `main`

Confirmed by both readings: the merge event and the commit on `origin/main` (12:44:03Z), never the `auto_merge` field. PR #8420, closed automatically by its `Fixes` trailer; `pm:dispatched` dropped.

**What shipped.** The two roles are split. `META_URL_TO_SINGULAR` in `@objectstack/spec/shared` is the URL-spelling contract, **derived** from `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` and unioned with every manifest spelling — so a newly *declared* type arrives already mapped and can never again fall through to the permissive plugin path, while nothing that resolved before resolves differently. `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` is untouched, so the authoring lint gains no `fields:` collection. The boundary additionally refuses an unrecognised plural of a declared type with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` rather than forwarding it, and that rule is **static** — it fires only when a spelling's singular is a type the platform itself declares, so a plugin-registered kind can never trip it whatever it is named or whenever it registers.

Both rulings shipped as ruled: the plural URL **folds** onto the singular's lock rather than earning a refusal of its own (measurements 1 and 2 deliberately converge), and the map is a **union** rather than a pure derivation — a pure one would have dropped six spellings naming plugin kinds with no registry entry (`themes`, `webhooks`, `connectors`, `sharingRules`, `ragPipelines`, `analyticsCubes`).

**Three things worth carrying forward.**

*The anti-vacuity arm cost nothing and was the strongest on the PR.* This card's own predecessor had left a test asserting the **defect** — `expect(res.status).toBe(200)` plus a row under `type='fields'` — with written instructions to flip it. Inverting that case proves the harness demonstrably reached the boundary before the fix: a fresh test asserting 403 could pass by never arriving. **Writing a known gap as a self-inverting pin is a pattern this lane should keep using.**

*The refusal is safe by construction, not by coverage.* A live-registry lookup would refuse a genuinely plugin-registered kind whenever registration had not happened yet — turning an authorization fix into a plugin-registration outage, a worse defect than the bypass. The static rule cannot do that. The sharp cases are pinned: `address`, `status`, `kudos`, `analysis`, `series` are ordinary words a plugin might name a kind, and a naive "looks plural" heuristic would refuse all five.

*The bypass was wider than this card claimed.* `seeds` now answers 422 because it is judged by the real `SeedSchema`. Before, an unmapped spelling had **no schema to be judged by**, so it sailed past validation as well as past authorization.

**Residues, both filed:** #8421 (a spelling that is not a plural of anything still takes the plugin path — same second-namespace class as #4432, but no authorization bypass, since it shadows no locked type) and #8424 (whether all five new `@objectstack/spec/shared` exports belong on the published surface — routed to `domain:spec`, not this seat's to rule).

**Correction on the record:** my sequencing comment above stated 26 registry entries under a "verified" heading. It is 27; the figure came from a regex over source rather than the built value. [Full correction here](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/7894#issuecomment-5280417883) — the unmapped set and both rulings are unaffected.
